content.text:
“Clean gold” is usually called **fine gold** or **24-karat gold**, and **99.9% purity** means it is almost entirely elemental gold, with only about **0.1% trace impurities**.

Why not 100%?

1. **Perfect purity is practically impossible**
   Even with modern refining, tiny amounts of other metals can remain, such as silver, copper, platinum-group metals, or iron.

2. **99.9% is a standard commercial grade**
   Gold labeled **999 fine** means **999 parts gold per 1,000 parts total material** — that is, **99.9% gold**. This is widely accepted for investment bars, coins, and bullion.

3. **Higher purity exists**
   Some gold is refined to **99.99%** purity, called **9999 fine**, and even **99.999%** in special cases. But **99.9%** is often enough for bullion and industrial purposes.

4. **Gold is often alloyed on purpose**
   Jewelry is rarely 99.9% gold because pure gold is very soft. It is mixed with metals like copper, silver, nickel, or palladium to make it harder and change its color.

So, **99.9% purity doesn’t mean gold is “dirty”** — it means it is refined to a very high standard, but not absolutely free of every trace impurity.
